source.text: Μὴ νομίσητε ὅτι ἦλθον καταλῦσαι τὸν νόμον ἢ τοὺς προφήτας· οὐκ ἦλθον καταλῦσαι ἀλλὰ πληρῶσαι·

records.literal_gloss: Not think that I came to abolish the law or the prophets; not I came to abolish but to fulfill;

en.L: Do not think that I came to abolish the law or the prophets; I did not come to abolish but to fulfill.
en.B: Do not suppose that I have come to do away with the law or the prophets. I have not come to do away with them but to fulfill them.
en.R: Do not think that I came to get rid of the law of Moses or the teachings of the prophets. I did not come to get rid of them. I came to make all that they said come true.

decisions.choice: the law or the prophets: the Scriptures
decisions.reason: "The law and the prophets" was a name for the Scriptures (7:12; 22:40).

decisions.choice: fulfill: bring to the full meaning and completion God intended
decisions.reason: In Matthew, Scripture is fulfilled when what it pointed to comes about (1:22; 2:15). Jesus both does what the law and prophets require and brings to completion what they promised; his teaching in 5:21-48 shows the law's full intent.

decisions.choice: the law of Moses, the teachings of the prophets; make all that they said come true
decisions.reason: Readable names the parts of Scripture and gives the main sense of "fulfill".

source.text: ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἕως ἂν παρέλθῃ ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ἡ γῆ, ἰῶτα ἓν ἢ μία κεραία οὐ μὴ παρέλθῃ ἀπὸ τοῦ νόμου, ἕως ἂν πάντα γένηται.

records.literal_gloss: Truly for I say to you, until pass away the heaven and the earth, iota one or one stroke not not will pass away from the law until all things happen.

en.L: For truly I tell you, until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota or one stroke will pass away from the law until all things take place.
en.B: Truly I tell you, as long as heaven and earth last, not one tiny letter or even part of a letter will vanish from the law until all of it comes about.
en.R: I tell you the truth, as long as heaven and earth last, not even the smallest letter or mark will be taken out of the law. It will stay until everything in it has happened.

decisions.choice: truly: Jesus's solemn "amen" before a saying
alternatives: a response to someone else's words
decisions.reason: "Amen" usually ends a prayer to agree with it. Jesus puts it first to vouch for what he is about to say.

decisions.choice: iota, stroke: the smallest letter and the smallest mark of a letter
decisions.reason: The iota stands for the Hebrew yod, the smallest letter. The stroke is the small hook that tells one Hebrew letter from another.

decisions.choice: until all things take place: until all that the law points to has come about
alternatives: until the end of the world only
decisions.reason: The second "until" can mean the same as the first, or point to what Jesus came to fulfill (5:17).

source.text: ὃς ἐὰν οὖν λύσῃ μίαν τῶν ἐντολῶν τούτων τῶν ἐλαχίστων καὶ διδάξῃ οὕτως τοὺς ἀνθρώπους, ἐλάχιστος κληθήσεται ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν· ὃς δ’ ἂν ποιήσῃ καὶ διδάξῃ, οὗτος μέγας κληθήσεται ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Whoever then breaks one of the commandments these the least and teaches thus the men, least will be called in the kingdom of the heavens; whoever but does and teaches, this one great will be called in the kingdom of the heavens.

en.L: So whoever breaks one of the least of these commandments and teaches {{gender:people|men}} to do so will be called least in the kingdom of the heavens; but whoever does [them] and teaches [them], this one will be called great in the kingdom of the heavens.
en.B: So anyone who loosens even the smallest of these commandments and teaches others to do the same will be called least in the kingdom of heaven. But anyone who obeys them and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
en.R: So if anyone breaks even the smallest command and teaches other people to do that, that person will be the least important in the kingdom of heaven. But anyone who obeys the commands and teaches others to obey them will be great in the kingdom of heaven.

decisions.choice: breaks: sets aside, treats as not binding
decisions.reason: The verb is related to "abolish" in 5:17. It means loosening a command, by disobeying it or teaching that it does not apply.

decisions.choice: these commandments: the commands of the law, as Jesus interprets them
decisions.reason: "These" points back to the law of 5:17-18. What follows (5:21-48) shows how Jesus reads it.

decisions.choice: least, great: rank within the kingdom
decisions.reason: Both are "in the kingdom". The saying is about standing there, not about entry, which 5:20 takes up.

source.text: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐὰν μὴ περισσεύσῃ ὑμῶν ἡ δικαιοσύνη πλεῖον τῶν γραμματέων καὶ Φαρισαίων, οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν.

records.literal_gloss: I say for to you that if not abounds of you the righteousness more [than] the scribes and Pharisees, not not you will enter into the kingdom of the heavens.

en.L: For I tell you that unless your righteousness exceeds [that] of the scribes and Pharisees, you will never enter the kingdom of the heavens.
en.B: For I tell you, unless your righteousness goes far beyond that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.
en.R: I tell you, you must be more righteous than the teachers of the law and the Pharisees. If you are not, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.

decisions.choice: righteousness: doing God's will
alternatives: a right standing given by God
decisions.reason: As in 5:6 and 5:10, righteousness is a life that does what God requires.

decisions.choice: exceeds the scribes and Pharisees: deeper, from the heart, not more rules
alternatives: more careful keeping of more rules
decisions.reason: The scribes and Pharisees were known for strict keeping of the law. The examples that follow (5:21-48) show a righteousness that reaches to anger, desire, truth and love of enemies (compare 23:23-28).

decisions.choice: the teachers of the law
decisions.reason: As in 2:4, Readable says what the scribes were.

source.text: Ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐρρέθη τοῖς ἀρχαίοις· Οὐ φονεύσεις· ὃς δ’ ἂν φονεύσῃ, ἔνοχος ἔσται τῇ κρίσει.

records.literal_gloss: You heard that it was said to the ancients, Not you will murder; whoever but murders, liable will be to the judgment.

en.L: You have heard that it was said to the ancients, 'You shall not murder; and whoever murders will be liable to the judgment.'
en.B: You have heard what our ancestors were told: 'Do not commit murder. Whoever commits murder must answer for it in court.'
en.R: You have heard that God's law told people long ago, 'Do not murder anyone. Anyone who murders will be judged.'

decisions.choice: it was said to the ancients: the law given to Israel at Sinai, as it was taught
decisions.reason: The dative most likely means "to" the generation at Sinai. The words are the command (Exodus 20:13) and a summary of the penalty (Exodus 21:12), as they were taught and heard in the synagogues.

decisions.choice: liable to the judgment: answerable before a court
decisions.reason: The judgment here is a court that tries cases of murder (Deuteronomy 16:18). Jesus goes on to judgment by God (5:22).

decisions.choice: you have heard ... but I say to you: the pattern of six sayings
decisions.reason: Each of the six sayings (5:21-48) sets the law, or a common reading of it, beside Jesus's own teaching. He goes deeper than the letter, as 5:17-20 says.

decisions.choice: our ancestors
decisions.reason: Balanced says whom Jesus's Jewish hearers would understand.

source.text: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ὀργιζόμενος τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ ἔνοχος ἔσται τῇ κρίσει· ὃς δ’ ἂν εἴπῃ τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ· Ῥακά, ἔνοχος ἔσται τῷ συνεδρίῳ· ὃς δ’ ἂν εἴπῃ· Μωρέ, ἔνοχος ἔσται εἰς τὴν γέενναν τοῦ πυρός.

records.literal_gloss: I but say to you that everyone being angry with the brother of him liable will be to the judgment; whoever but says to the brother of him, Raca, liable will be to the council; whoever but says, Fool, liable will be into the Gehenna of the fire.

en.L: But I say to you that everyone who is angry with {{gender:a brother or sister|his brother}} will be liable to the judgment; and whoever says to {{gender:a brother or sister|his brother}}, 'Raca,' will be liable to the council; and whoever says, 'Fool,' will be liable to the Gehenna of fire.
en.B: But I tell you that anyone who is angry with {{gender:a brother or sister|his brother}} will have to answer for it in court. Anyone who says to {{gender:a brother or sister|his brother}}, 'You empty-head,' will answer to the high council. And anyone who says, 'You fool,' will be in danger of the fire of hell.
en.R: But I tell you, if you are angry with {{gender:a brother or sister|your brother}}, you will be judged. If you insult someone and call them worthless, you will have to stand before the highest court. And if you call someone a fool, you will be in danger of the fire of hell.

decisions.choice: brother: a fellow member of God's people, man or woman
decisions.reason: In Matthew "brother" is often a fellow believer or fellow Israelite (18:15, 21; 23:8). The command applies to women as well as men.

decisions.choice: Raca: an Aramaic insult, "empty-head"; fool: one who rejects God
decisions.reason: Raca is an Aramaic word of contempt. "Fool" in Scripture can mean a person without sense or one who denies God (Psalm 14:1). Both treat another person with contempt.

decisions.choice: the council: the Sanhedrin; Gehenna: the place of final judgment by fire
decisions.reason: The Sanhedrin was the highest Jewish court in Jerusalem. Gehenna was the valley of Hinnom south of Jerusalem, where children had been sacrificed (Jeremiah 7:31), and its name became a name for the fire of God's judgment.

decisions.choice: the three steps: anger and contempt are as serious as murder before God
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the language of courts in rising order, from the local court to the council to God's judgment, to show that anger itself is under judgment.

decisions.choice: angry with a brother, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: angry with a brother without cause, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "without cause". Early manuscripts lack it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: You empty-head (B); call them worthless (R); the fire of hell (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Aramaic word and the place name. Balanced and Readable translate them.

decisions.choice: {{gender:a brother or sister|his brother}}
decisions.reason: The command covers women and men, so the inclusive form is the default.

source.text: ἐὰν οὖν προσφέρῃς τὸ δῶρόν σου ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον κἀκεῖ μνησθῇς ὅτι ὁ ἀδελφός σου ἔχει τι κατὰ σοῦ, ἄφες ἐκεῖ τὸ δῶρόν σου ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου καὶ ὕπαγε πρῶτον διαλλάγηθι τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου, καὶ τότε ἐλθὼν πρόσφερε τὸ δῶρόν σου.

records.literal_gloss: If therefore you offer the gift of you at the altar and there remember that the brother of you has something against you, \v 24 leave there the gift of you before the altar and go first be reconciled to the brother of you, and then having come offer the gift of you.

en.L: So if you are offering your gift at the altar, and there you remember that {{gender:your brother or sister|your brother}} has something against you, \v 24 leave your gift there before the altar and go, first be reconciled to {{gender:your brother or sister|your brother}}, and then come and offer your gift.
en.B: So if you are bringing your offering to the altar and there you remember that {{gender:a brother or sister|your brother}} has something against you, \v 24 leave your offering there in front of the altar. Go and make peace with {{gender:them|him}} first, and then come back and offer your gift.
en.R: So suppose you are about to give your gift to God at the altar in the temple. Then you remember that {{gender:a brother or sister|a brother}} is upset with you because of something you did. \v 24 Leave your gift there by the altar. Go and make things right with {{gender:that person|him}} first. Then come back and give your gift to God.

decisions.choice: your gift at the altar: an offering brought to the temple in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The gift is a sacrifice given to a priest at the altar of the temple. Galileans had a journey of several days to reach it, which sharpens the command to go back first.

decisions.choice: has something against you: has a grievance because you wronged them
decisions.reason: The one who comes to worship is the one at fault. Being reconciled matters more to God than the offering (Hosea 6:6, quoted in 9:13).

decisions.choice: make peace with (B); make things right with (R)
decisions.reason: Everyday words for reconciliation.

decisions.choice: the altar in the temple; give your gift to God
decisions.reason: Readable says where the altar was and to whom the gift is given.

source.text: ἴσθι εὐνοῶν τῷ ἀντιδίκῳ σου ταχὺ ἕως ὅτου εἶ μετ’ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ, μήποτέ σε παραδῷ ὁ ἀντίδικος τῷ κριτῇ, καὶ ὁ κριτὴς τῷ ὑπηρέτῃ, καὶ εἰς φυλακὴν βληθήσῃ·

records.literal_gloss: Be agreeing with the opponent of you quickly while you are with him on the way, lest you hand over the opponent to the judge, and the judge to the officer, and into prison you will be thrown;

en.L: Come to terms quickly with your opponent while you are on the way with {{gender:them|him}}, lest the opponent hand you over to the judge, and the judge to the officer, and you be thrown into prison.
en.B: If someone is taking you to court, settle with {{gender:them|him}} quickly while you are still on the way there. Otherwise your accuser may hand you over to the judge, the judge may hand you over to the guard, and you may be thrown into prison.
en.R: Suppose someone is taking you to court. Make things right with that person quickly, before you get there. If you do not, that person may take you to the judge. The judge may give you to the guard, and you will be put in prison.

decisions.choice: your opponent: someone taking you to court, probably over a debt
decisions.reason: The word is a legal one. Prison for debt kept a person until the debt was paid (18:30).

decisions.choice: a picture of the coming judgment as well as everyday advice
decisions.reason: The saying is sound advice in itself, but placed after 5:22 it also warns that there is little time to be reconciled before God's judgment.

decisions.choice: the situation first, then the advice
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable set out the case before saying what to do.

source.text: ἀμὴν λέγω σοι, οὐ μὴ ἐξέλθῃς ἐκεῖθεν ἕως ἂν ἀποδῷς τὸν ἔσχατον κοδράντην.

records.literal_gloss: Truly I say to you, not not you will come out from there until you pay the last quadrans.

en.L: Truly I tell you, you will never get out of there until you have paid the last quadrans.
en.B: Truly I tell you, you will not get out until you have paid {{units:the last penny|the last quadrans}}.
en.R: I tell you the truth, you will not get out until you have paid {{units:every last cent|the last quadrans}}.

decisions.choice: quadrans: the smallest Roman coin
decisions.reason: A quadrans was a quarter of a copper as, a sixty-fourth of a denarius, which was a day's wage for a laborer. The debt must be paid in full.

decisions.choice: {{units:the last penny|the last quadrans}} (B); {{units:every last cent|the last quadrans}} (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the modern smallest coin by default, with the original coin as the alternative. Literal keeps the original coin.
